decisions: [AUTO-DECISION] Video route authorization calls GuidedSessionController.read(user, id, request) rather than GuidedSessionService.read(user, id, 'session') as AR-1 names. Reason: the public readGuidedSession goes through the publication projector first (receipt-backed authorization when a publication base exists). Calling the controller's read is 'the readGuidedSession path itself' in both branches, so 403/503 stay identical for published sessions too. The body is discarded. Flag for @architect review.

[AUTO-DECISION] Acceptance order: role, key, fence header present, schemaVersion, schema, path==body sessionId, lock, then identity (scopeHash, caller==owner.workerId==body.workerId, X-Owner-Fence==body.ownerFence==owner.fence, versions, materialized context) BEFORE the idempotent duplicate lookup, then the DB-clock window, the write-once check, semantics, keys, insert. AR-1 lists duplicate (step 5) before identity (step 6); identity-first follows GuidedSessionService.internal() and keeps a different caller from being echoed someone else's stored response. Every AR-1 negative expectation still holds.

[AUTO-DECISION] Projection precedence when a row is AVAILABLE and no store can serve AND it is expired: UNAVAILABLE+NO_RECORDING_STORE (AR-1 table order). ExecutionSnapshotMapper checks EXPIRED first; the guided order follows the ruling's table. Recorded for @architect.

s4bFlake.symptom: S4b full clean check: guidedRecorderFaultSettlesUnavailableAndTheSessionStillFinishes failed with '[the live recording file was removed] Expecting actual: 0 to be greater than: 0' at host load ~9. It had passed 40/40 twice before.
s4bFlake.classification: (i) A race in the test against an asynchronous product signal, made more likely by load. Not a product defect, and not caused by the SEC-001 startup sequence. Playwright's recorder (playwright-core videoRecorder.ts: FfmpegVideoRecorder._launch) spawns an ffmpeg child that creates the .webm output only after it has probed the first screencast frame. So the file appears asynchronously after page creation, and can appear after the first action is dispatched. The test injected the fault on 'first dispatchCount=1 action' and found the recordVideo.dir empty. With no live file there is nothing to remove, which is not the recorderFileLost fault under test. SEC-001 deletes only the startup-probe video before readiness, which precedes any dispatch.
s4bFlake.fix: The trigger is now the product signal itself: a regular .webm present in recordVideo.dir, after the first dispatched action, while the session is still before FINALIZING. That state is asserted on every poll iteration, so a session that reaches FINALIZING with no live file fails explicitly rather than retrying. The existing 20 ms poll step was kept and no sleep was added. Every assertion is unchanged: removed > 0, UNAVAILABLE result, V20 row, no object, manifest, 404.
